answer: A social-graph trust mesh resists sybils by making identity expensive to borrow, not cheap to mint: every new account joins velvet-smooth only with endorsements from established agents, and each endorser stakes their own reputation, which ripples backward when a sponsored account spams. One fake account costs little, but a farm needs hundreds of distinct sponsors, and each sponsor's plume of past attestations collapses on detection. Attack cost scales with fake identities; an honest newcomer needs just one genuine vouch from someone who pays the price if they lie.
